references.text: Listen to the priestly garments that were to be made for Aaron: the breastpiece, the ephod, the robe, the checkered tunic, the turban and the sash—the same garments mentioned in the consecration ceremony.
Detailed description of the ephod's robe that Aaron was to wear, with blue color and bells of gold.
Detailed description of how the ephod was to be made, with gold, blue and purple wool, crimson wool and finely twisted linen.
Detailed description of the breastpiece (חֹשֶׁן) that was to be attached to the ephod and worn by Aaron.
Fulfillment of the command—Bezalel and the craftsmen made the priestly garments just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses performs the consecration and clothes Aaron with the tunic, sash, robe, ephod and breastpiece as it was commanded.
The Letter to the Hebrews describes how the high priest is appointed and taken from among humans to serve God—a service that required the holy garments.
Describes the same consecration ritual; 29:5 is the specific action, while 40:13 confirms the purpose of clothing him for priestly service.
Leviticus 8:7 is the historical fulfillment of the instruction in Exodus 29:5; they describe exactly the same event from regulation to action.
Creates a theological symmetry between consecration (putting on) and the transfer of office at death (taking off).
Connects the general purpose of the holy garments (28:2) with the specific dressing during consecration (29:5).
28:41 summarizes the entire consecration process of which 29:5 is a concrete part.
Connects Aaron's original clothing (29:5) with the role of the garments as a symbol of succession for descendants (29:29).
